findings.title: The dispatched worker role and serial compatibility manifest are incomplete
findings.cause: The blender-bpy skill omits the required worker role and the serial manifest omits the new test identities at the fixed artifact.
evidence: B1.8 independently reproduced the role/manifest failures against the fixed artifact and returned a repair commit with 36 scoped tests passing.
The fixed artifact predates that repair.
findings.impact: The package does not dispatch its Blender worker with the required profile and cannot satisfy repository compatibility admission.
findings.smallest_repair: Land B1.8's role and generated serial-manifest repair without changing the workflow behavior.

findings.title: Repository validation applies a superseded prose-only workflow rule
findings.cause: tools/validate_support/structure.py retains a blanket workflow-composition rule that rejects package-private scripts and schemas outside an old browser-game allowlist, while the current custom-workflow-authoring owner explicitly permits contained references, scripts, package metadata, and nested items.
evidence: The repository validator exits 1 on the 3d-browser-game scripts and JSON schemas with the message that a workflow contains only SKILL.md and reference prose.
C:/Users/danhm/.orchflows/lib/docs/custom-workflow-authoring.md permits these exact package-private boundaries and fixtures.
tools/validate_support/structure.py defines COMPOSITION_PROTOCOL_ALLOWLIST only for browser-game and applies validate_composition_admission to other workflow packages.
findings.impact: A package shaped according to the current owner contract cannot pass repository admission.
findings.smallest_repair: At the validator owner, retire or narrow the dated blanket rule and grade documented contained package paths through the existing compiler/containment checks; do not delete required executable evidence or add a new package-name exception.

findings.title: Default Three.js presentation is not measurable and the collector asserts zero perturbation
findings.cause: The native canvas attribution samples pixels after presentation. A normal default Three.js context has preserveDrawingBuffer=false, so the sampled buffer is cleared; only a hand-built preserveDrawingBuffer=true fixture with an artificial 8 ms cadence qualifies. The collector writes measurement_perturbation=false without a measured control despite synchronous readPixels.
evidence: C:/Users/danhm/.codex/worktrees/784d/orchflows-public/.orch-notes/native-performance-20260906 records the default case as N=120, C=0, callback_count=120, one repeated hash.
The positive native case changes the renderer contract to preserveDrawingBuffer=true and adds an 8 ms sampling delay.
example-workflows/3d-browser-game/scripts/performance_collect.mjs stores measurement_perturbation=false as a constant.
findings.impact: The required default Three.js live performance cell cannot qualify, and accepted timing could be materially changed by its measuring loop.
findings.smallest_repair: Observe presentation at a seam where the default buffer is valid or use another native attribution source, quantify the collector against a no-measurement control, and qualify default-positive, deliberate-stall-negative, plus three warm 60-second runs.

findings.title: Evidence-index promotion can be forged and typed coverage is not consumed
findings.cause: validateEvidenceIndex checks only the literal validator name and sha256 syntax of promotion.result_identity; it never recomputes the receipt. Generic JSON entries can satisfy gate evidence IDs without semantic or schema validation, and traceability/capture relations are not checked against their frozen sources and declared cells.
evidence: .orch-notes/promotion-probe/index-forged-promotion.json uses a 64-zero result identity and validate_evidence.mjs exits 0.
tests/test_3d_browser_game_play.py itself uses the same zero identity as a passing promoted index.
validateGate checks that evidence IDs exist but does not require gate-specific kinds for hard gates or scores.

A traceability document can contain one invented row; no consumer compares rows to the hashed brief/amendments. Capture matrix cells require capture IDs, but the consumer does not compare each capture's state, viewport, or DPR to its cell.
findings.impact: An index can claim promotion and complete prompt, visual, and gameplay coverage without proving those claims.
findings.smallest_repair: Compile and apply the shipped schemas, recompute a portable canonical promotion receipt, require typed evidence per gate claim, compare traceability rows with the frozen authorities, and match each capture to its matrix cell.

findings.title: Failed command labels qualify as adaptive actual play
findings.cause: validatePlaySession infers observation and adaptation from command type and ordering, not successful replies or observed state. It does not schema-admit the record or require the promised timing, snapshots, screenshots, DOM/state, console errors, or harness-bound transcript identity.
evidence: .orch-notes/play-classification-probe.mjs submits observe, key, and stop replies whose statuses are all error; validatePlaySession exits 0 with status=valid and adapted=true.
example-workflows/3d-browser-game/scripts/validate_evidence.mjs sets observed/adapted before checking reply success.
findings.impact: A fabricated or entirely failed transcript can establish both maker-independent play and adaptive evidence.
findings.smallest_repair: Schema-validate the full play record, require harness-owned digest/browser/timing data, and derive observation/adaptation only from successful, timestamped, meaningful facts around successful ordinary input and a recorded adaptation rationale.

findings.title: Performance repetition is counted globally instead of per frozen scenario
findings.cause: validateGate filters every animated result together, accepts any total of at least three, then requires all animated results to have one global signature. It has no declared performance plan or scenario-coverage comparison.
evidence: example-workflows/3d-browser-game/scripts/validate_evidence.mjs checks animated.length >= 3 and one signature after removing run identifiers.
No validator input enumerates the representative and worst-case scenario matrix required by the specification.
findings.impact: Three convenient repeats can omit required scenarios, while correct evidence for multiple scenarios is rejected.
findings.smallest_repair: Require a frozen performance plan and group evidence by declared cell/scenario, with three warm 60-second runs for every required animated cell.

findings.title: The outside probe accepts arbitrary event labels and does not validate either gate
findings.cause: outside_probe.mjs runs a caller-selected command and classifies a transcript from event type labels alone. It neither uses the package-owned build/serve/browser harness nor calls validateGate.
evidence: .orch-notes/outside-fake-probe.mjs prints four bare event objects: ready, observe, key, stop.
.orch-notes/outside-probe-index.json was legitimately promoted against the fixed HEAD.
outside_probe.mjs exits 0 and reports observed=true and ordinary_input=true for those labels.
findings.impact: The workflow can claim an outside ordinary-input close without booting or interacting with the game and without a valid core or final verdict.
findings.smallest_repair: Use a package-owned bounded build/serve/harness bound to HEAD, require successful timestamped browser facts, and validate both promoted gate records before close.

findings.title: The Blender job runner can promote a worker's self-declared validation
findings.cause: blender_asset_job.py copies job.validation into the worker result, blender_job_runner.py accepts inline pass labels and optional external reports, and the job's declared inputs/budgets/inspection surface are not closed or fully enforced. The result also lacks the actual Blender executable identity. validateAssetManifest has stronger independent checks, but final-gate admission does not require a manifest and the runner can report complete before that consumer runs.
evidence: The targeted test test_complete_outputs_require_hash_bound_external_validators exits 0 while its fake worker supplies inline pass labels and no external validator reports, then asserts promoted=true, status=complete, gaps=[].
blender_asset_job.py copies the job validation object rather than running Khronos or target GLTFLoader.
The probe job/test omits a closed scene allowlist and enforceable budgets; inspection does not cover the full required transform, texture, normal, armature, clip, pose, and collider surface.
findings.impact: Unvalidated, over-budget, or structurally wrong production assets can be reported complete and later omitted from final gate evidence.
findings.smallest_repair: Remove validation verdicts from worker-controlled input, execute pinned Khronos and target GLTFLoader in fresh bounded processes, require their hash-bound reports and actual tool identities, and enforce a complete job/manifest/inspection contract before promotion.

findings.title: Final acceptance does not prove the core-to-art ordering
findings.cause: validateGate(final) requires only the current artifact/index, traceability, rubric, capture matrix, play sessions, and performance cells. It does not require an accepted core verdict/baseline, concept-art provenance, asset manifests, descent from the accepted core, or affected-core regression evidence.
evidence: The final fixed_inputs definition in gate-verdict.schema.json has no core baseline, concept set, manifest set, or core-reproof field.
validateGate's final branch never searches the evidence index for those records.
The public SKILL text states the correct ordering, but the acceptance consumer cannot establish that it happened.
findings.impact: A final pass can bypass the fundamental core gate and production provenance, allowing art to mask weak or untested gameplay.
findings.smallest_repair: Require a typed accepted core verdict as a declared ancestor, bind concept and asset records to that baseline, require closed asset manifests, and re-run affected core proof before final promotion.

findings.title: Complaint and successor history is erasable
findings.cause: The run-record and traceability schemas are never consumed by validateEvidenceIndex or validateGate. A pass checks only that the current verdict has empty complaints and gaps; there is no predecessor ledger, lawful status-transition, closure evidence, invalidation, or successor-lineage comparison.
evidence: loadEntry has special consumers for play sessions, performance, asset manifests, captures, and capture matrices, but none for run-record, traceability, or gate-verdict schemas.
validateGate ends by accepting an empty current complaints array and never loads a prior verdict or run record.
run-record.schema.json calls itself append-only but represents only one mutable snapshot and has no predecessor identity.
findings.impact: A repair cycle can delete unresolved complaints, lose invalidations, or rewrite its two-round history while still passing the final consumer.
findings.smallest_repair: Schema-admit run records, traceability, and verdicts; require predecessor-bound successor records; preserve every complaint ID with a lawful transition and closure evidence; reject missing, reopened, or rewritten history.

findings.title: The pinned Ajv version has a known $data ReDoS advisory
findings.cause: package-lock.json pins Ajv 8.17.1, affected by GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6 below 8.18.0 when $data is enabled.
evidence: Root observed npm ci succeed and npm audit exit 1 with the advisory and a fixed 8.20.0 release.
A scoped source search exits 1 with no $data use and no Ajv compile/import in the current package scripts.
findings.impact: The current package does not expose the advisory trigger, so correctness at the fixed identity is not presently blocked; the planned schema-admission repair would make Ajv reachable.
findings.smallest_repair: Update the direct pin and lockfile to a fixed Ajv release before adding schema compilation, then run schema tests and npm audit.

verified_non_findings.evidence: validateGate requires the exact core/final constant sets and rejects every score below the frozen floor of 3.
The reviewed workflow and standards are operationally direct and no secrets, credentials, or unsafe credential instructions were found.
